tasks.gr11-momentum-t2: Topic: Momentum and Impulse. Cover momentum as a vector (p = mv, SI unit: kg·m/s), impulse (J = FΔt = Δp), the impulse-momentum theorem, the law of conservation of momentum for isolated systems (Σp_before = Σp_after), elastic collisions (KE conserved), inelastic collisions (KE not conserved), and perfectly inelastic collisions (objects stick together). Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate momentum and impulse, apply conservation of momentum to one-dimensional collisions, classify collision types, and interpret force-time graphs for impulse.
tasks.gr11-projectile-motion-t2: Topic: Vertical Projectile Motion. Cover free-fall under gravity (g = 9.8 m/s² downward), the kinematic equations for vertical projectiles (v = v_i + gΔt, Δy = v_i Δt + ½gΔt², v² = v_i² + 2gΔy), upward-launched projectiles (maximum height where v = 0, symmetry of flight), downward projectiles, and qualitative effect of air resistance. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate time of flight, maximum height, and velocity at any point for both upward and downward projectiles; interpret velocity-time graphs; and apply kinematic equations systematically.
tasks.gr11-electrostatics-t2: Topic: Electrostatics. Cover types of electric charge (positive and negative), conservation of charge, Coulomb's law (F = kQ₁Q₂/r², k = 9 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²), the electric field (E = F/q = kQ/r²), electric field lines (direction from positive to negative, density indicates field strength, lines never cross), and superposition of fields. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate electrostatic forces and field strengths, determine net force or field from multiple charges, sketch electric field patterns, and apply Coulomb's law to charge and distance problems.
tasks.gr11-electric-circuits-t2: Topic: Electric Circuits. Cover conventional current (I = Q/Δt), potential difference (V), resistance, Ohm's law (V = IR), series circuits (same current everywhere, V_total = ΣV_i, R_total = ΣR_i), parallel circuits (same voltage across branches, I_total = ΣI_i, 1/R_total = Σ1/R_i), emf and internal resistance (ε = V_terminal + Ir), and power dissipation (P = VI = I²R = V²/R). Ask Grade 11 learners to analyse series and parallel circuits, calculate equivalent resistance, determine terminal voltage under load, and solve power problems in multi-component circuits.
tasks.gr11-refraction-snell-t2: Topic: Refraction, Snell's law, critical angle and total internal reflection. Cover refractive index n = c/v with c = 3,00 × 10⁸ m·s⁻¹, that frequency stays constant while speed and wavelength change, Snell's law n1 sin θ1 = n2 sin θ2 with angles from the normal, bending towards or away from the normal, the critical angle sin θc = n2/n1 (light going from a larger to a smaller n), conditions for total internal reflection, and optical fibres and endoscopes. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate angles, speeds and critical angles, always stating the refractive indices needed.
tasks.gr11-diffraction-t2: Topic: Wavefronts and diffraction. Cover wavefronts (points in phase), Huygens' principle, diffraction as spreading at a small aperture or around a sharp edge, that the degree of diffraction increases with λ/a, and the single-slit pattern explained qualitatively by constructive and destructive interference of secondary wavelets (bright central band widest). Ask Grade 11 learners to reason about which wave or gap diffracts more and to calculate λ = v/f and λ/a.
tasks.gr11-ideal-gases-t2: Topic: Ideal gases. Cover the kinetic molecular theory, ideal and real gases (real gases are closest to ideal at high temperature and low pressure), Boyle's law P1V1 = P2V2, Charles' law V1/T1 = V2/T2, Gay-Lussac's law P1/T1 = P2/T2 with temperature in kelvin (T = °C + 273), the combined law P1V1/T1 = P2V2/T2, and PV = nRT with R = 8,31 J·K⁻¹·mol⁻¹ (P in Pa, V in m³, T in K). Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate with given values, always stating R and any units conversion needed.
tasks.gr11-moles-concentration-t2: Topic: Moles, gas volumes and concentration. Cover n = m/M, the molar volume 22,4 dm³·mol⁻¹ at STP (273 K and 101,3 kPa), gas volume ratios from a balanced equation, concentration c = n/V in mol·dm⁻³ (volume in dm³), and empirical and molecular formulae from percentage composition and molar mass. Use atomic masses from the data sheet (Cl = 35,5). Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate moles, masses, volumes, concentrations and formulae.
tasks.gr11-stoichiometry-t2: Topic: Stoichiometry. Cover mole ratios from balanced equations, mass-to-mass calculations, the limiting reagent (compare moles divided by the coefficient), the mass of excess reagent, percent yield (actual/theoretical × 100) and percent purity of a sample. Balance every equation used. Ask Grade 11 learners to calculate with given masses and molar masses.
